LESSON: INTRODUCTION TO GEOGRAPHY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY
Strand: Practical Geography Introduction to Geography 8 Map Reading and Interpretation 1
Topic 1.1: Introduction to Geography
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Introduction to Geography, part of Practical Geography Introduction to Geography 8 Map Reading and Interpretation 1 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY.

Key inquiry question: How does the study of Geography impact on people’s lives?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Brainstorm on the meaning and branches of Geography and make class presentations. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC, and be allowed extra time to express their views on the meaning and branches of Geography.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Brainstorm on the meaning and branches of Geography and make class presentations. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC, and be allowed extra time to express their views on the meaning and branches of Geography.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Introduction to Geography together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: The skill of effective communication as the learner discusses the

relationship between Geography and other disciplines and presents in class

• Critical Thinking: The skill of interpretation and inference as the learner brainstorms on the meaning and

branches of Geography

• Creativity and Imagination: The skill of making connections as the learner creates posters on careers related

to Geography

• Digital literacy: The skill of interacting with digital technology is enhanced as learners use digital resources to

examine the importance of studying geography and write short notes.

Values:
● Unity: Learner cooperates as they discuss in groups the relationship between Geography and other disciplines

and makes class presentations

● Responsibility: Learner remains accountable as they use digital resources to establish the importance of

studying Geography

● Integrity: Learner exhibit honesty as they carry out research within the school on a selected Geographical

topic.

● Respect: Learners express patience as they brainstorm on the importance of statistics in Geography and make

presentation in class.
